newsitem.title: USA: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - supply tapers, Fed tightens?.
newsitem.headline: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - supply tapers, Fed tightens?.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds mainly were unchanged in late trade on Friday as the market waited to see if the Federal Reserve would meet its expectations by raising interest rates at its March 25 meeting.

After a series of warnings by the central bank Chairman Alan Greenspan that he was prepared to fight inflation pre-emptively, traders said municipal bond levels largely reflected the anticipated 25-basis point increase.
"The way I see it, the Fed tightening is already priced in to the market," a trader said.

This prospect, along with the Easter holiday on March 30, were cited as two of the factors that were causing new issuance to slide next week to about $1.9 billion, down sharply from nearly $3.7 billion this week.
Next week's negotiated offerings total $1.5 billion in 40 sales, with a $600 million Hawaii general obligation deal through Smith Barney Inc. topping the the list.
On the competitive side, 44 sales totaling $347 million are on the schedule, with a $45 million Oakland, Calif., deal on Wednesday the largest.

Traders also noted that after a few robust weeks of new supplies, players have a bit of an inventory overhang that might take a little while to disappear. "I think dealer shelves are pretty heavy right now," another trader said.

This week's sales included a $525 million general obligation bond offering by California, which fetched just five basis points off the triple A scale, according to Nuveen Research, which said the narrow spread reflected the state's improving credit.

As has been the case for the past year or so, potential buyers typically have to sell old issues to make room for new ones because the municipal market has not been attracting big supplies of nw cash on a consistent basis. That money largely has been siphoned off by equities markets.
The secondary market saw its supplies firm, as the Standard and Poor's Corp Blue List, a yardstick of how much is on offer, totaled over $1.6 billion, a fairly strong level.
While there were a fair number of bid-wanted lists being circulated on Friday, traders said that the number of bonds being advertized for sale had tapered off from levels seen earlier this week.

Actively quoted issues included Texas State Turnpike Authority Dallas North Thruway Revenues of January 2023, which pay a 5-1/4 percent coupon, and were bid at 5.79 percent, NET, down two basis points.
And Delaware River Port Authority of Pennsylvania and New Jersey Revenues of January 2026, which pay a 5-1/2 percent coupon, were offered at 5.70 percent, NET, unchanged.

In the futures markets, the June municipal bond futures ended down two ticks at 113-7/32, while the June Treasury bond futures gained two ticks to 108-23/32. This left the MOB spread at plus 144 ticks.
